newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Swedish debt yields rose on Monday marginally despite stronger foreign markets.
The crown was somewhat weaker against the mark but gained against the dollar.
"Sweden is doing worse than foreign markets. I think we see profit-taking in the wake of the spread against Germany decreasing so much lately," one trader said.
The spread between Swedish and German ten-year bonds increased by six basis points to 93. Most traders said profit-taking was the reason.
"The spread has decreased by some 30 basis points during the past month. It is reasonable that we see a small recoil," one trader said.
The ten-year bond yields rose one basis point to 6.48 percent while the six-month T-bill rate inched up two basis points to 4.11 percent.
The crown was somewhat weaker against the mark to 4.4170 from 4.4070 late Friday because of a generally stronger mark. The crown gained to 7.6997 against the dollar from 7.7303.
The next domestic focus will be Wednesday's state borrowing forecast. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1019
